text.p: The Commonwealth Bank of Australia's stockbroking susbsidiary, Commonwealth Securities, said on Friday it had launched an on-line stockbroking service.

In what it described as first for an Australian bank, Commonwealth Securities said local or overseas investors could now both view live share prices and trade in Australian shares over at its Internet site (www.comsec.com.au).
Local and overseas investors started trading on-line as soon as the system went live, it said.
"The bank has pioneered the use of technology to make access to the sharemarket as simple as possible for all Australians," Commonwealth Securities director Paul Rickard said.
He said Internet trading complemented Share Direct, Commonwealth Bank's phone based share broking service.
Rory Collins, director of information and marketing at the Australian Stock Exchange (ASX), was quoted in a Commonwealth Bank news release as welcoming the move.
"The ASX supports any initiative which broadens the understanding to the sotckmarket and improves access to it for retain investors," Collins said.
"The Internet lends itself as an ideal medium for stockbroking given the immediacy of information demanded by investors and the interaction it provides," Collins said.
"We expect to see significant and growing levels of business over the Internet," he said.
